finding.title: Remove or explicitly justify AppLogger.setupFlutterErrorHandlers — dead code duplicating crashlytics_bootstrap.dart's live handlers
finding.why: Grepping every .dart file in the repo shows AppLogger.setupFlutterErrorHandlers is referenced nowhere except its own definition and its 3 unit tests in logger_test.dart. Production's bootstrap chain (bootstrap.dart:40) installs FlutterError.onError/PlatformDispatcher.onError exclusively via bootstrapCrashlyticsHandlers in app/bootstrap/crashlytics_bootstrap.dart — a completely independent implementation of the same responsibility that also forwards to Crashlytics (setupFlutterErrorHandlers only forwards to Talker). A maintainer reading logger_test.dart's 3 green tests would reasonably believe this is the production error-handling path; if some future refactor swaps main.dart's wiring back to this method for 'simplicity', fatal-crash reporting silently stops reaching Crashlytics while Talker logs keep looking healthy, and the existing green test suite would not catch it since it only ever exercises the unused copy.
finding.recommendation: Delete AppLogger.setupFlutterErrorHandlers and its 3 tests, or — if it's meant as a documented fallback for contexts without Crashlytics wired — rename it and add a comment cross-referencing crashlytics_bootstrap.dart so the duplication is intentional and visible rather than accidental drift.
acceptance_criteria: grep -rn 'setupFlutterErrorHandlers' lib/ returns only its own definition, or a caller with a comment explaining the split from crashlytics_bootstrap.dart
No test exercises a code path unreachable from main.dart's actual bootstrap chain

finding.title: Six leftover migration re-export shims in features/sync/ are unused by production code and violate Rule 2's 'only providers.dart barrel' clause
finding.why: Rule 2 states the providers.dart barrel is 'the only sanctioned re-export file. Do not add other barrel/re-export files.' These six are bare `export '...';` shims (or, for sync.dart, an empty library-only file with zero exports) left over from moves labelled W1.4/W1.7/W1.8 in their own comments. Grepping every .dart file in the repo: restore_providers.dart, device_restore_screen.dart, and sync.dart have zero importers anywhere, even in tests. merge_rules.dart, profile_scoped_preference_keys.dart, and device_restore_service.dart are imported only by test files, never by lib/ production code, which already uses the canonical core/app paths directly. sync.dart's comment additionally claims 'the legacy sync stack is being deleted in Wave 2... After deletion, sync infrastructure lives in lib/core/sync/', which is stale -- OutboxSyncWriteFacade and LocalDataUploadService are the live, current replacement and were never meant to be deleted. A developer trusting this comment or grepping 'where is merge_rules defined' gets actively misleading signal.
finding.recommendation: Delete all six files; repoint the test files that still import the deprecated paths (merge_rules_test.dart, profile_scoped_preference_keys_test.dart, device_restore_service's story-acceptance tests) at their canonical locations, moving them to the AG-5-mirrored test path in the process.
acceptance_criteria: grep confirms zero remaining files under lib/features/sync/ that are bare export re-directs to core/ or app/.

merge_rules_test.dart and profile_scoped_preference_keys_test.dart import from lib/core/sync/merge/merge_rules.dart and lib/core/preferences/profile_scoped_preference_keys.dart respectively, at the AG-5-mirrored test path.

finding.title: Add the required `// keepAlive:` justification comment to Sacred Time's 6 keepAlive providers

evidence.quote:
@Riverpod(keepAlive: true)
LocationService locationService(Ref ref) => const LocationService();

finding.why: coding-standards.md SM-6 requires every keepAlive: true to carry an inline // keepAlive: comment; these 6 declarations (cities_provider.dart:7, sacred_location_provider.dart:12/17/123, sacred_windows_provider.dart:13/33) have nearby doc comments explaining rationale but none use the required tag, so a future audit grep for the literal marker (as SM-6's own Enforce plan proposes) would still flag all 6 as unjustified even though they are reasoned. This mirrors a repo-wide gap (only ~6/86 keepAlive sites in lib/ use the tag), not something unique to this feature.
finding.recommendation: Prefix each keepAlive declaration's existing rationale with the literal `// keepAlive: ...` tag so the future audit grep can find it.
acceptance_criteria: All 6 keepAlive providers in this batch carry a // keepAlive:-prefixed comment
A grep for 'keepAlive: true' paired with a check for the tag on the preceding line finds no gaps in this feature

finding.title: Override localDayClockProvider in track_detail_screen_test.dart to remove its wall-clock dependency

evidence.quote:
userDatabaseProvider.overrideWith((ref) => db),
    // Goal writes go through goalRepositoryProvider,

finding.why: TrackDetailScreen reads localDayClockProvider via _trackPaceCalcProvider (default = SystemLocalDayClock, real DateTime.now()). track_detail_screen_test.dart's _overridesFor list never overrides it, while every sibling file that mounts the same screen in this batch (track_detail_goal_stale_test.dart, edit_track_and_detail_l1_test.dart) does, with FakeLocalDayClock pinned to 2026-05-30. No current assertion in track_detail_screen_test.dart depends on paceCalc's output, so this isn't flaky today, but it's one inconsistent override away from date-dependent flakiness the moment someone adds an assertion that touches TrackInfoCard's pace-derived text (days-remaining, projected finish), and it's inconsistent with the established pattern in the same directory.
finding.recommendation: Add localDayClockProvider.overrideWithValue(FakeLocalDayClock(DateTime.utc(2026, 5, 30))) (or another fixed date) to _overridesFor, matching the sibling files.
acceptance_criteria: track_detail_screen_test.dart's _overridesFor includes a localDayClockProvider override with a fixed date

finding.title: Migrate switcherSheetPinGuardRequiredProvider to @riverpod codegen and move it to presentation/providers/
finding.why: This provider was added fresh in commit 2c346a77 ('AN-2 gate escalating actions... wave-B'), not part of the 121-usage legacy backlog the standard exempts — SM-1 explicitly says to count new additions. Every other provider in the same feature already uses @riverpod codegen (profile_providers.dart:129,137,147; active_profile_provider.dart:42). Because it's a manually-declared, non-family FutureProvider it is never autoDispose: once any widget reads it, it and its watch of profileListStreamProvider/activeProfileIdProvider stay alive for the app's remaining lifetime, not just while the switcher sheet is open. The doc comment's stated reason for going manual ('so tests can inject a known result without touching FlutterSecureStorage') doesn't require it — codegen providers are equally overridable in tests, as the neighboring codegen providers demonstrate.
finding.recommendation: Rewrite as an @riverpod FutureProvider<bool> under presentation/providers/, keeping the same override-based test seam.
acceptance_criteria: switcherSheetPinGuardRequiredProvider is annotated @riverpod and lives in lib/features/profiles/presentation/providers/
an2_switcher_pin_guard_test.dart's existing overrides continue to pass unmodified
No manually-declared top-level Provider/FutureProvider remains under presentation/widgets/ in this feature
